chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I was with Al-Reza (peace be upon him) regarding one of the needs, and I intended to leave to go to my house. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Come with me and spend the night in my presence.' So I went with him and entered into his house along with Al-Mu'tab. So he (peace be upon him) looked at his servants who were working with the clay in the animal enclosure, and other such work, and there was a black man with them who was not from them. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Who is this man with you?' So they said, 'He is helping us and we would give him something.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you agreed his wages with him?' So they said, 'No. He would be pleased from us with whatever we give him.' So he (peace be upon him) faced towards them to strike them with the whip, and was angered due to that with an intense anger. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Why are you taking it upon yourself?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have forbidden them from the likes of this many a time, to make anyone work with them until they agree his wages beforehand. And know that there is no one who would work for you anything without an agreed wages, and then you increase something for him three times over upon his wages, he would still think that you have been deficient in his wages; and when you agree his wages beforehand, then give his wages to him, he would praise you upon the loyalty. So if you were to increase it even by a grain, he would recognise that for you and view that you have given him more.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hiring workers without agreeing on wages beforehand?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *muqata'ah* (explicit wage agreement) as a prerequisite for valid employment, emphasizing that ambiguity in compensation leads to *ghabn* (perceived injustice) even if the actual payment is generous. Imam Al-Reza (AS) illustrates the psychological and spiritual dimensions of fair trade, noting that workers are keenly aware of whether they are being treated with precise justice or merely given a bonus, thereby linking economic transactions to moral integrity and social harmony.
